name: cvucsedit
description: Adds features to VS Code for loading, editing and saving Cabinet Vision User Created Standards

untrustedWorkspaces.description: UCS code is read from the Cabinet Vision SQL database named in your user settings, and saving a mirrored file writes back to it. The connection and mirror location settings are ignored when they come from an untrusted workspace. VS Code's own TypeScript support is limited until you trust the folder, so UCS:JS completion, hover, rename and find references stay unavailable; the standards list, UCS:M support and database sync work either way.

cvucsedit.Server.description: The Cabinet Vision database SQL server instance name

cvucsedit.Database.description: The name of the Cabinet Vision SQL database.

cvucsedit.AutoStart.description: Connect to Cabinet Vision automatically when a workspace opens. This only ever applies to a workspace where the extension has already been used: a workspace that has not connected before stays untouched until you run 'Cabinet Vision UCS: Connect'. Turn this off to start manually every time.

enumDescriptions: Mirror into a folder of the extension's own, outside all of your projects (see cvucsedit.MirrorPath). Open it with 'Cabinet Vision UCS: Open UCS Workspace'.
Mirror into the folder currently open, under cvucsedit.MirrorFolder.
cvucsedit.MirrorLocation.description: Where UCS code is mirrored as real files. Leave unset to let the extension decide per workspace: a workspace that already contains a mirror keeps using it, anything else uses the dedicated folder so that no UCS files or AGENTS.md changes appear in unrelated projects.

cvucsedit.MirrorPath.description: Full path of the dedicated mirror folder, used when cvucsedit.MirrorLocation is 'dedicated'. Empty means '<your home folder>/Cabinet Vision UCS'. Each database gets a subfolder of its own. Avoid a cloud synced folder such as OneDrive: the mirror tracks a live database.

cvucsedit.MirrorFolder.description: Folder name used when cvucsedit.MirrorLocation is 'workspace'. The folder ignores itself in git, and is what makes UCS code reachable by AI agents, search and standard JavaScript tooling. Deliberately not dot prefixed: some AI agent tools skip hidden folders when looking for context. An existing '.cvucs' folder is moved here automatically.

cvucsedit.WriteRootAgentFiles.description: Maintain a short block in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the root of the folder holding the mirror, pointing AI agents at it. Most agent tools only look for these files at the project root. In the dedicated mirror folder this is written straight away; in one of your own projects you are asked first, per workspace. Existing files are appended to between markers, never overwritten.

cvucsedit.WriteMirrorGitignore.description: Keep a .gitignore containing '*' in the mirror folder, so mirrored UCS code never appears in a git repository. Turn this off only if you intend to version the mirror yourself, and understand that git then writes to the live database: the file watcher cannot tell a checkout, merge, pull, stash pop or reset from a save, so anything that rewrites a file on disk is pushed to Cabinet Vision, one UPDATE per changed file, with no undo. A conflicted merge pushes its conflict markers too, and a branch cannot add or remove standards. Reading history ('git log', 'git show', 'git diff') is safe; restoring from it is not. Turning this off deletes the .gitignore if it is still the one we wrote; a file you have edited yourself is left alone.

cvucsedit.CheckJs.description: Report TypeScript diagnostics in mirrored UCS:JS files. Completion, hover, go to definition and rename work either way; enabling this also surfaces type errors, which can be noisy.

cvucsedit.DebugFolderSuffix.description: End of the folder path Cabinet Vision opens when it launches VS Code to debug a UCS, for example 'C:\ProgramData\Hexagon\CABINET VISION\CV 2025\Temp\UCSJS'. A window opened on a folder ending this way connects automatically and gets UCS:JS language support and the Cabinet Vision API on its plain .js files. Clear this to turn that off. Only the ending is matched, since the install path and version differ per machine.

Not connected to Cabinet Vision in this workspace.

Connecting mirrors your UCS code as real files. Choose where that folder goes with the `cvucsedit.MirrorLocation` setting - by default it is a folder of its own, outside your projects.
